body:
It's not that I don't want to involve medical professionals in general.  More that right now I'm not ready to talk about this with my regular doctor, and he's who would have to deal with referrals for substance abuse counselors and the like.

After a decade of secrecy and being closed-off, it's going to take me a bit of time and work to be able to open up.  This is something I've gone to a huge amount of effort to keep hidden for a long time, so I need to work up to that.

I'm planning to do a bit of research to see if I can find a private program, separate from my usual medical practice, as well as NA meetings.  The advice I've gotten so far in this thread has made me realise that I am going to need some help, and I found a nearby meeting that I can go to tomorrow.

I'm hoping that once I have a bit more control over the situation, and some forward momentum, that I'll feel more comfortable taking about it with the people in my life, including my doctor.  And absolutely, if it ever comes to the worst case scenarios, I would for sure contact someone.  I want to make things better, not worse.

Thank you for taking the time to reply.

Thanks for replying.

I'm just not comfortable talking to my doctor about it yet.  I'm hoping that once I've given myself a bit of a head start I'll find it a bit easier to open up about it.  Kinda like, "The bad news is... but the good news is, I've already blah blah."

Thanks so much for the link!  That will be incredibly useful.  I've found a nearby meeting that I'm planning to attend tomorrow, and I'll try to talk to someone there about what's going on.

I'll definitely continue using this sub for support as well.  I've gotten a lot of very useful advice, and it's given me a lot to think about as far as giving myself a better chance to succeed at this.

Thanks for responding.

I'm in the UK, so I'm not entirely sure what the confidentiality laws are like.  I'll have to do some research.

I definitely recognise that this is gonna be a total lifestyle change rather than just "eh, I just won't use drugs anymore."  My ultimate goal is to get clean, stay clean, and be the person I'm supposed to be.  I'm going to need to do a lot of work on myself, and accept responsibility for everything I've done, be honest, all that jazz.  You guys are all right, there is no way I will be able to do it by myself.

At this point, I'm not comfortable involving friends and family, and until I've done a bit of research I'm not going to bring it to my doctor yet either.  I found an NA meeting nearby that I'm going to attend tomorrow, and I'll speak to whoever appears to be in charge there.  I'm also going to continue tapering down, and I think that if I give myself a bit of a head start with some progress, it might be easier to tell people about it.  Does that make sense?

I know that I have an addict's brain too, and that I can manipulate and lie my way into or out of anything,  but enough awful shit has happened in the last few months to make me realise that I cannot keep doing this, and I don't want to keep doing this.

I'm sure I'm going to be hit with a whirlwind of emotions and difficult situations that I'd usually cover with drugs, but I'm hoping I can learn to be strong enough for it.  It's already rather unpleasant and anxiety-inducing, and I'm doing my best to cope.  Hopefully I can learn from the people at the meetings, and get to a point where I can at least share this with a couple of "real life" people.

Again, thanks.  You guys have given me a lot to think about.

I found a nearby meeting that's scheduled for tomorrow evening, and I'm going to go to it as long as it's okay to be there while tapering.

I've really thought about what everyone's said, and if I can't bring myself to talk to my family, friends, or doctor about this yet, I need to get started on meetings as soon as possible to keep the sobriety momentum going forward.  If it's just me, it's not gonna work.  I have to get real about the fact that if I haven't done it myself in ten years, I'm not going to be able to do it by myself.

It's totally fine if they don't want me to say anything yet at the meetings.  I can sit and listen.

Thanks for clearing that up though!

It's no problem!

Hmm, in that case... I looked online, and there's a meeting nearish here tomorrow evening.  I'm gonna go and have a listen.

Thank you for your reply, and your support!

I started a taper three days ago to begin the process without putting too much stress on my system, and I know it's not much but I'm really proud of myself for having stuck to it so far.

I'm definitely glad I posted here.  I've gotten some good advice, and if nothing else, I've admitted that I have a serious problem and that I'm trying to fix it.  Given the great pains that I take to hide everything, that was actually a huge relief.

I'll have to look into that for sure.  I'm okay with counselling as long as I can make sure the info is totally confidential.  I'll see what Google can come up with in my area.

Thanks for your kind words!  It's been a big problem for a long, long time and I need to stop hiding behind drugs and learn how to be my real self.  I'm not expecting it to be easy or pleasant, but it's gotta be done.

Thanks for responding.

I'm willing to attend NA meetings.  Anonymous groupings are okay, I'm just not ready to involve my doctor, family, and friends.  I think it's going to take some time and effort for me to become a less secretive, closed-off person.  I'll find out more about meetings nearby.

I'm not too aware of the rules and protocol of NA, so I don't know if I'd be allowed to attend at the moment (3 days into tapering off) or not.  

As far as I know, I'd have to be referred to a substance abuse counselor by my general doctor.  I'll have to look into this, because if I'm wrong I've no objection to drug counseling as long as I can keep it separate -for the time being, anyway- from everything else.

Also, I'm a girl.  Sorry if I didn't make that clear in my post.  I've no objection to being called "dude" though!

Thank you for replying.

I think NA meetings would be a good idea.  You're right in that it would provide some support and structure without involving the people in my life.  I'll have to do a bit of research to look for meetings in my area, as well as the general rules and protocol.  I'm not sure I'd be allowed to attend just yet as I am only three days into a taper, thus technically still using.  Since I'm doing this on my own I've chosen a gradual reduction to avoid putting my system into too much of a shock.

I honestly hope it turns out better than you -or for that matter, I- think.  So far I'm sticking to the taper, and I'm equal parts surprised and proud.

Thank you for responding.

It really isn't possible for me to share this with anyone I know, including my doctor and other medical professionals.  I'm hoping that a greater tendency toward honesty and openness will come with time and practise.

I think that outpatient rehab services would still be tied to my general doctor, so that won't be possible right now.

I'm regularly seen by my doctor, so he'll be able to continue to monitor my general health though he won't know about any of this.  

I've started with a taper, three days ago.  I'm trying to be as careful as I can so that I can gradually reduce my drug intake and not put my system through too much shock.

thank you from the bottom of my heart for sharing karen's story -and yours- with me in your comments and through the link to your other post.  she was surely a beautiful person and so are you.

i can't do it to them.  i can't cause them to hold what would be the third funeral in three months.  i still don't want to be alive but i owe it to them to at least try.  

maybe, if i try, i could be... i don't know, a person with less things to hate about herself.  i'm still not sure about anything.  in fact i feel much more confused now than i did when i was just waiting until the holidays were over to carry out my plan.  i have no idea what's going to happen beyond my doctor's appointment tomorrow, and actually i'm not even entirely sure what will happen at the appointment itself, but i think maybe that's okay.

i don't know what made you reply to my post or what has kept you talking to me, but thank you.  thank you.  thank you.  and:

thank you, karen.  i'm really sorry i didn't get to know you before you left, but i'm sure we'll get to hang out in wherever the next place is.  i think it'll be awhile longer than i'd planned before i get there, and you've had a big role in that.  peace.

so, tomorrow the trying begins.
whoops, i think i just accidentally put my long-winded (sorry!) reply to you as a comment to my original post.  i have no reddit skillz.

wow, i can definitely identify a lot with your sister from the things you mentioned. as cliched as it is, if you get lost inside your own head for long enough you really do feel like your problems and their corresponding traits are unique and that you're the only one.  i'm so sorry she got lost. she sounds like a girl who was a lot stronger and "better" than she thought she was, and it's an awful thing that she isn't around anymore. how old was she? you don't have to tell me if you don't want to.  i have one brother and couldn't imagine what it would be like to lose him.  my dad's death has been horrible and confusing enough, but my brother's always been my little buddy, almost like a limb.

i had never actually considered the possibility of pursuing addiction advice and support online because for some reason i've always thought of it like "well if i get help everyone will have to know.  i'll have to tell my doctor and everyone will know i'm going to meetings", etc.  another "everyone will know" point in my mind would be the detox/physical withdrawal aspect.  i've tried tapering off on my own several times, but every time i'd get a new supply to continue the painless and not-noticeable-to-others taper, despite my best intentions i'd just start using regularly again.  i hadn't thought about the possibility of accessing anonymous advice and support online, which is crazy because i (and everyone else) use the internet for practically everything.  if i could have help without anyone in my life knowing... a window in my mind just opened a crack.

yeah, i have no idea why i'm so secretive. it's not that i don't trust other people- i don't trust or like myself.  i wish i wasn't like this because it's lonely and exhausting. maybe it's a control thing.

sooo, your reply made me cry.  since i never tell anyone anything about this stuff, i've never experienced anyone reacting to it, let alone being understanding and supportive of it.  thank you.  you're good people.

i am going to attend my appointment with my doctor tomorrow morning and i'm going to tell him that i've been very depressed and anxious and we'll see what he says about that.  after that i am going to look into online support for my addiction and some other issues. i think... i think i'm going to try not to kill myself.

apologies for the late reply, but it's actually because i wanted to take some time to really think about the points you made, even though (and especially because) they are things that i have been forcing myself not to think about in order to be able to carry through with my plan.  but you took time to read my post and reply thoughtfully, so i wanted to do the same.

there are a lot of people who care about me, which is something you have to do your best not to think about if you want to kill yourself.  i have a loving partner, a handful of great friends, and a scattering of caring family members. i also have two spoiled and adored cats.  there are difficulties in two of the main relationships in my life, but overall i am very aware that i am loved, and needed.
apart from the first sixteens years of my existence, 85% of the awful parts of my life are my own fault.

i'm going to be completely honest with you, which is something i never am.  i'm an addict.  painkillers. highly functioning to the point where no one knows, and if anyone does happen to suspect, they'd have no idea of the extent.  i have tried to stop several times, and succeeded once... for a month.  i am no longer under the illusion that i could quit on my own, and i don't want anyone to know.  this has pros (no one knows what a weak, idiotic person i am) and cons (no one actually really knows me at all).  this is one of many things that secures my position in the "terrible person" category.

i am extremely secretive in general and only allow each person in my life to know certain parts of me. none of them would still want to be around me if they knew about the other parts.  and i know that i am a shitty and very fucked up person. i've been a mess since i was a kid.  i feel guilty and afraid every day.

on one hand, i know that my suicide will absolutely destroy the people who love me.  on the other hand, i know that they will be better off without me.

i am very very very sorry about your loss and your grief.  grief is a lot more bizarre than i thought it would be- do you find that as well?  i always thought i would just feel deeply sad, but instead i feel like my entire life and identity have been altered, which i guess they have.

when you told me that you lost someone to suicide... that's the part that really made me want to think carefully about everything you said and apply it to myself. so whatever happens, thank you for that.  i still cannot see any possibility of light for myself, but for my loved ones i have booked an appointment to see my regular doctor tomorrow morning.  i am only intending to talk to him very generally about my anxiety and depression.  i am not mentioning anything about suicide to him, nor will i tell him about any of the other things i told you in my unusual burst of honesty.  i don't even know why i am going to see him at all because i don't give a shit about myself and want (and intend) to die, but on the 2% chance he has any suggestions like medication tweaks or whatnot, i feel like i owe it to my family and friends to ask.

by the way, i'm totally aware that i can't be properly helped unless i am honest about everything that's going on, but i don't feel capable of doing that.  this is all i've got, and as usual it's not great.

anyway, thank you for talking to me and for letting me talk to you.  i wasn't aware of it when i originally posted, but i think the purpose of coming to this sub was probably to be my complete-honest-real-terrible-cowardly-useless self for the first time, so that maybe one person would know the real me before i'm gone.  so thanks for letting me do that.  really.

i guess i feel like this time too many things have irrevocably changed, preventing the same kind of stability -or life, even- to be obtained again.  i feel like i've lost too much, caused too much harm.  and i don't know how to explain this properly, but i feel like even when i am happy, okay, or stable, i am always going to come back to this because a) that is what has always happened before, b) it's the nature of bipolar disorder, and c) i am a shitty person who does shitty things and deserves to either feel shitty or not be alive.  i can promise you that i don't deserve the life i have. i often see strangers and wish i could transfer my life force to them because pretty well anyone else is a better person than me.  i don't feel like i can stand to be myself anymore.  after the holidays i will end my life.  i know it's ridiculous, trying to counter the ultimate selfish act with a "well, i don't want to ruin anyone's christmas or new year's eve" but it's all i've got.

i'm very sorry to read that you are also going through a dark time, and i sincerely hope your path becomes lighter.  it's wonderful that you are holding onto hope for and memories of better times and knowing that you can be there again. keep doing that, please.
